  • Short Answer Type Questions

questions.question: Describe the basic structure of the Constitution.
questions.solution_html:
• The basic structure of the Constitution refers to the fundamental principles and framework
  • that cannot be altered or amended by the Parliament. It includes features such as the supremacy
  • of the constitution, separation of powers, federalism, secularism, and the protection of
  • fundamental rights.

questions.question: Distinguish between single and dual citizenship
questions.solution_html:
• In dual citizenship, each person is a citizen of both country and state. But in single
  • citizenship, a person has only the citizenship of the country; there is no separate state
  • citizenship.

questions.question: Analyse the importance of Article 32 and 226 of the Indian Constitution.
questions.solution_html:
• Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court of India and Article 226 allows the High Courts to
  • issue appropriate writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights. Writ is an order of the court
  • by which the court directs an individual official or an authority to do an act or abstinence.
questions.final_answer: by which the court directs an individual official or an authority to do an act or abstinence

questions.question: Fundamental rights are available against the State and not against private individuals. Explain.
questions.solution_html:
• The rights which are given to the citizens by way of fundamental rights are a guarantee
  • against state action as distinguished from violation of such rights from private parties. Private
  • action is sufficiently protected by the ordinary law of land.
questions.final_answer: action is sufficiently protected by the ordinary law of land

questions.question: Fundamental duties are considered as a code of conduct for the citizens of India. Examine
questions.solution_html:
• Article 51-A of the Indian Constitution specifies a code of fundamental duties for citizens.
  • They are statutory duties. Its main object is to remind every citizen that, while enforcing
  • fundamental rights, he must also be conscious of his fundamental duties.
questions.final_answer: fundamental rights, he must also be conscious of his fundamental duties

questions.question: Freedom of speech and expression guaranteed under the Constitution is not an absolute right. Explain
questions.solution_html:
• Freedom of speech and expression guaranteed under Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution is
  • not an absolute right.It is subject to the following restrictions contained in Article 19(2)such as
  • (i) Security of the State (ii) Friendly relations with foreign states (iii) Public order
  • (iv) Decency or Morality (v) Contempt of Court (vi) Incitement to an offence (vii) Integrity &
  • sovereignty of India

questions.question: Analyze how the Directive Principles reflect the ideals of the Indian Constitution.
questions.solution_html:
• The Directive Principles of State Policy contained in Part IV of the Constitution set out the
  • aims and objectives to be taken up by the state in the governance of the country. It contains a
  • list of socio- economic rights and freedoms which the state is expected to secure for the people
  • through suitable legislative enactments.

questions.question: Describe the Constitutional provisions relating to service conditions of High Court Judges
questions.solution_html:
• High Court judges are appointed by the President of India in consultation with the Chief
  • Justice of India and the Governor of the State concerned. Their term of office is up to 62 years.
  • A judge may be removed from his office by the process of impeachment (before he attains the
  • age of 62 yrs.). Qualifications: (i) Citizen of India (ii) Advocate for ten years in a High Court
  • or held a judicial office for ten years.
questions.final_answer: or held a judicial office for ten years

questions.question: Identify the role of Vice-President of India
questions.solution_html:
• Vice President is elected by an electoral college consisting of all the members of Rajya
  • sabha and Lok sabha at a joint session by secret ballot. He is the ex-officio chairman of Rajya
  • Sabha. He presides over the meetings of the Rajya sabha and whenever any vacancy occurs in
  • the office of the President, he acts as President until a new President is elected.
questions.final_answer: the office of the President, he acts as President until a new President is elected

questions.question: Distinguish between Union list and State list.
questions.solution_html:
• The union list is a list of items given in the seventh schedule of the Constitution of India on
  • which Parliament has exclusive power to legislate. State legislature is empowered to make
  • laws with respect to those matters enumerated in the state list. Parliament is also permitted to
  • make laws with respect to any matter in the state list if it is approved by the Rajya sabba by 2/3
  • majority in the interest of the nation.
questions.final_answer: majority in the interest of the nation

questions.question: Enumerate the rights of the members of the legislature with respect to freedom from arrest
questions.solution_html:
• Members of the legislature are entitled to immunity from arrest during the session of the
  • legislature and also for 40 days before and after the session of the legislature in civil
  • proceedings. However this privilege is not available in a criminal charge or contempt of court
  • or preventive detention; Arrest must be informed to the presiding officer of the House.
questions.final_answer: or preventive detention; Arrest must be informed to the presiding officer of the House

questions.question: Analyse the role of Governor for the declaration of state emergency.
questions.solution_html:
• Governor is the constitutional head of the state. The President, on receipt of a report from
  • the Governor of the state or otherwise, satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the govt. of
  • the state cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the constitution; he may
  • issue proclamation for the state emergency.
questions.final_answer: issue proclamation for the state emergency

questions.question: Discuss in detail, the salient features of the Indian Constitution
questions.solution_html:
• i) The lengthiest Constitution in the World ii) Parliamentary form of Government
  • iii) Unique blend of rigidity and flexibility iv) Fundamental rights v) Directive Principles of
  • State Policy vi) Federation with strong centralizing tendency vii) Adult suffrage
  • viii) Independent judiciary ix) Secular State x) Single citizenship xi) Fundamental duties.
questions.final_answer: viii) Independent judiciary ix) Secular State x) Single citizenship xi) Fundamental duties

questions.question: Analyze the scope of Public Interest Litigation in the context of the remedial measures provided by Article 32 of the Indian Constitution.
questions.solution_html:
• Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court to issue appropriate writs for the enforcement of
  • fundamental rights. Writ is an order of the court by which the court directs an individual
  • official or an authority to do an act or abstinence. Types: (i) Habeas Corpus (ii) Mandamus
  • (iii) Certiorari (iv) Prohibition (v) Quo warranto. Earlier, only persons whose fundamental
  • rights are violated have the right to move to the court for the enforcement of their fundamental
  • rights. Now, public interest litigation is permitted at the instance of public spirited citizens for
  • the enforcement of constitutional and legal rights of others who because of their poverty or
  • other reasons are unable to approach the court. Any member of the public can approach the
  • court for enforcing the constitutional or legal right of other persons.
questions.final_answer: court for enforcing the constitutional or legal right of other persons

questions.question: The freedom of speech and expression guaranteed by the Constitution is subject to limits. Analyse.
questions.solution_html:
• Freedom of speech and expression guaranteed under Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution
  • means the right to express one’s own views, opinion, ideas etc. freely by words of mouth
  • writing, painting, pictures or any other mode. It connotes the liberty to propagate the views of
  • other people. It implies the right to propagate or publish the views of others and thus the
  • freedom of press is included in this expression. It includes freedom of circulation and
  • propagation of ideas. But this right is not an absolute right. It is subject to the following
  • restrictions contained in Article 19(2) of the Constitution, such as (i) Security of the state
  • (ii) Friendly relations with foreign states (iii) Public order (iv) Decency or morality
  • (v) Contempt of court (vi) Incitement to an offence (vii) Integrity & sovereignty of India.
questions.final_answer: (v) Contempt of court (vi) Incitement to an offence (vii) Integrity & sovereignty of India

questions.question: "The Supreme Court is the highest court of appeal in the country". Discuss the statement with special reference to the appellate jurisdiction of the court. ***
questions.solution_html:
• Supreme Court is the highest court of appeal in India. Supreme Court entertains appeal
  • from any judgement, decree or final order of the High Courts in civil, constitutional and
  • criminal matters and also from any judgement, decree, sentence or order in any case made by
  • any court or tribunal in India. It is the final interpreter and guardian of the Constitution..
  • Appellate Jurisdiction of the Court: (a) appeal in constitutional matters (b) appeal in civil cases
  • (c) appeal in criminal cases (with and without a certificate from High Court) (iv) Appeal by
  • special leave (Art. 136)
